meta.provenance: Concepts and trap structures derived from KMF/Gremlin's GRE source set; every stem, all numbers, all options and all explanations are original. No source text reproduced.

questions.question: For each of the years 2021 and 2022, the population of Town K increased by 25 percent during the year. If the population was 500,000 on December 31, 2022, approximately what was the population on January 1, 2021?
questions.explanation: Two successive 25 percent increases multiply the starting population by 1.25 twice: P x 1.25 x 1.25 = P x 1.5625. Setting that equal to 500,000 gives P = 500,000 / 1.5625 = 320,000.
questions.trap: Students reason that two 25 percent increases are undone by one 50 percent decrease and answer 250,000. Percent changes compound multiplicatively, so reversing them means dividing by 1.5625, not subtracting half.

ets_rescore.prev_note: 'Approximately' on exact answer is a nit.

questions.question:
A brand of floor cleaner is sold in two bottle sizes. The small bottle holds 3/8 as many millilitres as the large bottle and sells for 1/2 the price of the large bottle.
Quantity A: The price per millilitre of the cleaner in the small bottle
Quantity B: The price per millilitre of the cleaner in the large bottle
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Let the large bottle hold V millilitres and cost P. The small bottle then holds 3V/8 and costs P/2. Its price per millilitre is (P/2) divided by (3V/8), which is (P/2)(8/3V) = 4P/(3V). The large bottle's price per millilitre is P/V. Since 4/3 is greater than 1, the small bottle costs more per millilitre, so Quantity A is greater.
questions.trap: Students note that the small bottle is cheaper in absolute terms and conclude it is the better value. The price fell to one half but the volume fell to three eighths — a steeper drop — so the unit price actually rose.

questions.question: Solution P contains a percent salt by weight. Solution Q contains b percent salt by weight. If 4 kilograms of solution P are mixed with 6 kilograms of solution Q to yield 10 kilograms of solution R, what percent of the weight of solution R is salt?
questions.explanation: Solution P contributes 4 x (a/100) kilograms of salt and solution Q contributes 6 x (b/100), so solution R holds (4a + 6b)/100 kilograms of salt within 10 kilograms of solution. The percent by weight is that amount divided by 10 and multiplied by 100, which simplifies to (4a + 6b)/10.
questions.trap: Students average the two concentrations as (a + b)/2, ignoring that the solutions contribute unequal weights. With 4 kilograms of one and 6 of the other, the result is pulled toward solution Q.

rationale.B: inverting each concentration — dividing the weight by the percent instead of multiplying (retained from original)
rationale.C: reciprocal of B's error in the other direction — dividing each percent by its weight rather than multiplying (retained from original)
rationale.D: averaging the two concentrations unweighted, (a + b)/2, ignoring that the 4 kg and 6 kg contributions are unequal
rationale.E: multiplying by 10 instead of dividing by it when converting the salt weight to a percent of 10 kg (retained from original)

questions.question:
Last year the value of one share of a certain fund increased by 12 percent from January to July, and increased by 45 percent from January to December. What was the percent increase in the value of one share from July to December of last year?

Give your answer to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: Take the January value as 100. A 12 percent increase puts the July value at 112, and a 45 percent increase from January puts the December value at 145. The rise from July to December is 145 - 112 = 33, measured against the July value of 112: 33/112 = 0.2946..., which rounds to 29 percent.
questions.trap: Students subtract the two given percentages and answer 33, treating both as if they shared the same base. The July-to-December increase is measured against the July value of 112, not against January's 100.

questions.question: One day, at a filling station in Country P, diesel was selling for 90 pesos per gallon. On that day, 1 peso could be exchanged for 0.06 dinars. If diesel was being sold at an equivalent rate in Country Q, which of the following calculations gives the approximate price, in dinars, of one liter of diesel in Country Q that day? (1 gallon is approximately 3.785 liters.)
questions.explanation: Start from 90 pesos per gallon. Converting the currency means multiplying by 0.06 dinars per peso, giving (90)(0.06) dinars per gallon. Converting the volume means dividing by 3.785, since one gallon is 3.785 liters and a per-liter price covers less fuel than a per-gallon price. The result is (90)(0.06)/3.785.
questions.trap: Students multiply by 3.785 instead of dividing, reasoning that a gallon is larger than a liter so the number should grow. A liter is less diesel, so it must cost less — the per-liter figure has to come out smaller than the per-gallon figure.

questions.question:
In 2022, the price of a certain commodity increased by 40 percent from March 1 to April 1 and then decreased by n percent from April 1 to May 1. If the price on May 1 was greater than the price on March 1, which of the following could be the value of n?

Indicate all such values.
questions.explanation: Let the March price be 100. After a 40 percent increase it is 140. A decrease of n percent leaves 140(1 - n/100), and this must exceed 100. So 1 - n/100 > 100/140 = 5/7, which is about 0.7143, giving n/100 < 2/7, or n < 28.57. Of the options, 12, 22 and 28 satisfy this; 30 and 35 do not.
questions.trap: Students assume a 40 percent rise is cancelled by a 40 percent fall and take the cutoff to be n = 40, admitting 30 and 35. The decrease is applied to the larger post-increase price, so a smaller percentage is enough to erase the gain — the real cutoff is about 28.6 percent.

questions.question: Working at their respective constant rates, machine R can produce 24,000 bolts in 8 hours and machine S can produce 24,000 bolts in 4 hours. If the two machines work simultaneously and independently at their respective constant rates, they would produce a total of 24,000 bolts in how many minutes?
questions.explanation: Machine R produces 24,000 / 8 = 3,000 bolts per hour, and machine S produces 24,000 / 4 = 6,000 bolts per hour. Working together they produce 3,000 + 6,000 = 9,000 bolts per hour. The time for 24,000 bolts is 24,000 / 9,000 = 8/3 hours, and 8/3 x 60 = 160 minutes.
questions.trap: Students average the two times as (8 + 4)/2 = 6 hours, or add them. Rates add when machines run simultaneously; times do not. A quick sanity check settles it — the combined time must be shorter than the faster machine alone, which is 4 hours.

questions.question:
Yesterday, 30 percent of the guests who had checked in to Hotel Y departed before 10 A.M., and 60 percent of the remaining guests departed before noon.
Quantity A: The percent of the guests who had checked in to Hotel Y yesterday who had not departed before noon
Quantity B: 25%
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Take 100 guests. Thirty depart before 10 A.M., leaving 70. Of those 70, sixty percent depart before noon: 0.60 x 70 = 42. That leaves 70 - 42 = 28 guests who had not departed before noon, so Quantity A is 28 percent. Since 28 is greater than 25, Quantity A is greater.
questions.trap: Students add the percentages, conclude that 90 percent had departed, and answer 10 percent — applying the 60 percent to all guests rather than to the 70 percent still present. The second percentage is taken of the remainder, not of the original total.
questions.ets_note: Two-step percent-of-remainder with one wording wrinkle; reads medium, not hard.

questions.question:
Last season and this season there were both novices and veterans on a certain team. This season there are k fewer novices and k fewer veterans on the team than there were last season, where k > 0, and there are fewer veterans than novices on the team.
Quantity A: The percent decrease from last season to this season in the number of novices on the team
Quantity B: The percent decrease from last season to this season in the number of veterans on the team
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Both groups fell by the same absolute amount, k. A percent decrease is k divided by last season's count, so the group that started smaller shows the larger percent decrease. Both groups dropped by the same k, so whichever group is smaller this season was also smaller last season — that is the veterans. Dividing the same k by the smaller base gives the larger percentage, so Quantity B is greater.
questions.trap: Students see equal absolute decreases and select 'the two quantities are equal'. A percent change depends on its base, so an identical drop of k is a larger percentage of the smaller group.

questions.question: A car rental company offers a 25 percent discount on the standard daily rate, and then charges an 8 percent service fee on the discounted rate. If a customer rented a car for one day and paid a total of d dollars, including the service fee, what is the standard daily rate, in dollars?
questions.explanation: Let the standard daily rate be r. The discounted rate is 0.75r, and the 8 percent service fee multiplies that by 1.08, so the customer pays 0.75r x 1.08 = 0.81r. Setting 0.81r = d gives r = d/0.81.
questions.trap: Students net the two percentages into a single 17 percent reduction and answer d/0.83, or they multiply rather than divide and answer 0.81d. The discount and the fee apply in sequence to different bases, so their effects multiply to 0.81 — and recovering the original rate means dividing by that factor, not multiplying.

questions.question:
In a quality inspection, 150 crates of bolts were examined; each crate contained 40 bolts. For each crate, the ratio g of the number of defective bolts in the crate to the total number of bolts in the crate was recorded. The number of defective bolts per crate varied from 1 to 9, inclusive.
Quantity A: The sum of the 150 values of g
Quantity B: The sum of the squares of the 150 values of g
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Each value of g is a number of defective bolts divided by 40, so g ranges from 1/40 = 0.025 up to 9/40 = 0.225. Every value therefore lies strictly between 0 and 1, and squaring a number strictly between 0 and 1 always makes it smaller. Each of the 150 squared values is less than the value it came from, so the sum of the squares is less than the sum. Quantity A is greater.
questions.trap: Students assume squaring makes a number larger, which holds only for values above 1. Since no crate has more than 9 defective bolts out of 40, every g is well below 1 and every square shrinks.

questions.question:
A ball is dropped from a height of 4 meters and bounces repeatedly. After each bounce it reaches a height that is 70 percent of its previous height. If the height of the ball after the nth bounce is less than 25 centimeters, which of the following could be the value of n?

Indicate all such values.
questions.explanation: The height after n bounces is 4(0.70)^n meters, and 25 centimeters is 0.25 meters, so the condition is 4(0.70)^n < 0.25, or (0.70)^n < 0.0625. Working up the powers: 0.70^7 = 0.0824, still too large, and 0.70^8 = 0.0576, which is below 0.0625. So the condition first holds at n = 8 and holds for every larger n. Of the options, 8 and 9 qualify.
questions.trap: Students treat the 30 percent lost per bounce as if it accumulated by subtraction and estimate that three or four bounces are enough. The heights form a geometric sequence, each term 0.70 times the last, and it takes eight bounces to fall below one sixteenth of the drop height.
questions.ets_note: Requires repeated multiplication by 0.7 to eight powers; no structural shortcut.
